newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian leu seen plunging after elections - banker.
newsitem.headline: Romanian leu seen plunging after elections - banker.

text.p: An executive with a top Romanian bank said on Wednesday the leu currency was artificially being held high and would plunge after next month's general election, but the central bank dismissed his forecast.
Other traders also predicted the leu was bound to fall after November 3 presidential and parliamentary elections but said the decline would not be a sharp one.

Alexandru Ghiba, First Vice-President of Bancorex told the newspaper Adevarul the leu was vastly overvalued at its current rate of 3,295 to the dollar. He said its true value was closer to 5,500 to 6,000 and would eventually slide to between 10,000 and 12,000 within a year.
"The explosion will happen soon," he said. "Probably in few weeks, almost certainly after elections."
On Wednesday, the leu was quoted at 3,295/3,305 to the dollar on the interbank market and at 3,570 by licensed money changing bureaux.
Bancorex, one of the four market making dealer banks handling almost half of Romania's foreign trade, also posted the leu at 3,295/3,305 against the greenback.
"Pressure (on the leu) is already high, and things can no longer stay as they are," Ghiba told Adevarul.
A central bank statement said Ghiba's forecast was a "false prophecy. It will not come true."
Traders suggested Ghiba was excessively pessimistic. But they agreed the leu's real range reached 4,500 to the dollar.
"His estimate would mean that Romania had lost control over the economy," said one trader with a broker bank.
The leu has been gradually slipping against the dollar from 2,600 in January.
Economists have accused Romania's leftist government of trying to keep the leu high ahead of the elections.
Analysts said Romania's problems stem from a move in March stripping all but four banks of their local dealer licences to try to peg the currency at a high level.
The International Monetary Fund has suspended loan tranches to Romania to express its disagreement the move. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
